output.headline: Amends Achieve Academy's facilities agreement to let EPIC share its Hawthorne campus space for 2019-20
output.summary: This amendment to a Proposition 39 facilities use agreement lets EPIC temporarily share space with Achieve Academy, a charter school, within Achieve Academy's existing space at the Hawthorne campus. The amendment covers July 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020. No dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Buys 12 kitchen workstations from Kruger International for up to $36,002.77

money.evidence: at a cost not to exceed $36,002.77

output.summary: Kruger International will furnish and install 12 workstations for the new Central Commissary Building kitchen. The $36,002.77 limit includes a 10% contingency (a reserve for unexpected costs) of $3,000. The text says the contractor was selected under Public Contract Code section 20111(b) and Government Code section 53060, and the work period began December 12, 2019, before this vote.

output.headline: Pays Valley Relocation & Storage up to $55,000 to move Fremont High into its new building
output.summary: Valley Relocation & Storage will provide move-in services and move items from storage into the new building for Phase II of the Fremont High School new construction project. The $55,000 includes a $1,099.60 contingency (a reserve for unexpected costs). Work is scheduled from February 13 to June 30, 2020, using Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Accepts $50,000 from Warriors Community Foundation for K-1 reading help and family literacy kits
output.summary: The district receives a $50,000 grant. Half is $5,000 for each of five schools to pay for reading interventions and books for kindergarten and first graders. The other $25,000 pays for family literacy kits with leveled books, flashcards and activities for parents. The grant covers October 1, 2019 to June 30, 2020 and is routed through the County of Alameda.

output.headline: Joins the Oakland Literacy for All Coalition at no cost to the district
output.summary: The district becomes an active member of a coalition of nonprofit, community and direct-service groups working to make sure every Oakland child learns and loves to read. The agreement can last up to four years from approval and costs the district nothing.

output.headline: Declares a district vehicle surplus and allows the district to dispose of it
output.summary: The Board is declaring a vehicle from the Risk Management Department obsolete and surplus under state education law. This allows the district to dispose of it. The vehicle is listed in an exhibit that is not included in the official text, and no dollar amount is stated.

output.headline: Pays Star Elevator up to $25,000 to modify fire circuitry on Fremont High's elevator
output.summary: Star Elevator will provide labor and materials to change the fire service circuitry on the passenger elevator at Fremont High School, part of the school's new construction project. The $25,000 includes a $6,218.92 contingency (a reserve for unexpected costs). Work is scheduled from February 13 to June 30, 2020, and is paid from Measure J bond funds.

output.headline: Approves Board Policy 4144.5 on whistleblower protection for employees (second reading)
output.summary: The Board approves Board Policy 4144.5, a personnel policy on whistleblower protection. The title marks this as the second reading, and the consent item text does not describe the policy's contents.

output.summary: DSF Commercial Flooring was the lowest responsive and responsible bidder for flooring maintenance services, including minor repairs, at district sites. The $629,480 covers the whole period from February 13, 2020 to June 30, 2023. It is paid from the routine restricted maintenance account.

output.summary: Nor-Cal Moving Services will provide furniture and moving equipment for the relocation of Glenview Elementary School at the Santa Fe site, as part of the school's new construction project. The $27,000 includes a $3,687 contingency (a reserve for unexpected costs). Work is scheduled from February 13 to December 31, 2020, using Measure J bond funds.
